hero.subtitle: A living world. A hundred floors down. One question at the bottom.
hero.desc: A text RPG where the town keeps going when you log off. NPCs get married, have kids, get old, die. 100-floor dungeon. Seven gods who want to talk before you fight them. Five different endings. GPL licensed, totally free.

philosophy.title: WHY I MADE THIS
philosophy.subtitle: Notes from the developer
philosophy.lead: As a kid, I dialed into BBSes on a 14.4k modem. Usurper stuck with me over LORD and Trade Wars for its depth. In 2004, Jakob Dangarden released the Turbo Pascal source under the GPL, and that's what made this remake possible. I found it later and started Usurper Reborn in C# in 2024 to drop the 1990s hardware limits. It keeps the original dungeon, class system, team warfare and politics.
philosophy.world_desc: The living town is the part I most wanted to get right. The server runs the world simulation around the clock, whether anyone is online or not. Town NPCs have birthdays and distinct opinions. They marry on their own and raise children who grow into new townsfolk. Regular residents eventually die of old age, but story characters do not age. If you take a break, the town shifts before your next login. People you used to know might be gone, and you will meet new faces.
philosophy.ngplus_desc: Once you finish an ending, you can start New Game+ to play through the world again. The town NPCs slowly begin to recognize you across runs. Early on you only get a slight hint. By your third cycle, they ask why everything feels like it already happened. One ending breaks the loop instead. The five endings are not ranked by difficulty. They're five answers to the same problem. I don't think any of them is the right one.
philosophy.gods_desc: Seven corrupted gods are sealed inside the dungeon as boss encounters. Each one speaks to you before battle begins. Your dialogue choices during these conversations alter their stat modifiers and combat abilities. At the bottom of floor 100, the final god does not want to fight. He is tired. He asks you a question, and the choices you made throughout the game decide the ending.
philosophy.text_desc: People ask me a lot why it's a text game. I kept it text on purpose. That honors the original, and some scenes hit harder as text late at night than they would as a cutscene.
philosophy.closing: You play on a shared server where other players' actions change the same world. There are no ads, microtransactions or loot boxes, and the code is on GitHub under GPL v2 for you to read or fork.
philosophy.closing_play: You can play right now through a browser, SSH, telnet or a BBS.
r1.free_steam: The game is free and open source, so you can play in your browser, over SSH or telnet, or from GitHub release builds. The Steam version is the same game, and buying it is an optional way to support development.
features.title: WHAT'S IN IT
features.subtitle: The stuff the original had, plus everything I kept wishing it had back in the day.
features.npcs_desc: They've each got personality traits (like commitment, romanticism, aggression), goals, opinions, and memory of what you've done to them. They hold grudges. They remember stuff across NG+ cycles too, which gets weird.
features.lifecycle_desc: This is the part people seem to notice first. The NPCs actually get married, have children, grow old, and die. Their kids grow up into new NPCs. The population turns over. You might log in one day and your favorite shopkeeper is just... gone, and their kid is running the place now.
features.news_desc: There's a live news system that tracks everything happening in town. Marriages, deaths, births, assassinations, plagues, coming-of-age ceremonies. It all just happens on its own.
features.multiplayer_desc: You can play offline by yourself or hop on the shared server. The server runs the world sim 24/7. There's PvP, chat, a shared economy, and a leaderboard. Your actions show up in other players' news feeds.
features.dungeon_desc: Floors are generated deterministically, so the layout stays the same each visit and you actually learn the map. Seven god encounters. Six seals to find. Gets genuinely hard around floor 50+.
features.rpg_desc: 12 classes, 10 races, 75 spells. Romance system, marriage, kids. Court politics and throne challenges. Factions you can join or betray. 5 recruitable companions with their own quest lines. A PvP arena. Pretty much everything the original had, plus a lot more on top.

story.title: THE STORY
story.subtitle: This is the setup. It doesn't spoil anything past the first hour.
story.golden_desc: Seven gods once watched over the world. A god of war taught honor in battle, and a goddess of love blessed unions. A god of light kept truth. The legends call it a good time, but nobody alive saw it.
story.sundering_desc: Then came the Sundering. Something went wrong, but accounts disagree on whether mortal pride caused it or one god betrayed the others. All seven gods were corrupted and sealed underground. The war god lost his mind. The love goddess began to fade, and the god of truth went quiet.
story.avarice_desc: Centuries later, the old gods are stories told to scare children. The dungeon that holds them is the Halls of Avarice. Adventurers go there for gold. Some who go deep start hearing voices from something very old. It calls them further down.
story.you_desc: You start at level 1 with 2,000 gold. You pick a race and a class. You fight in the dungeon and make friends or enemies in town. You can take part in politics, and you can marry. A strong enough character can challenge the king for the throne. The gods talk to you before each fight. What you say changes that fight, and the choices you make across the whole game decide which ending you get.
gods.title: THE SEVEN OLD GODS
gods.subtitle: Seven broken gods are trapped down in the dungeon. Each one stood for something once, and you decide what happens to them.
gods.maelketh_desc: You meet him first down on floor 25. He stood for honorable combat in the past, but now he fights without knowing why. What you say to him before the fight changes how it goes.
gods.veloura_desc: She's fading on floor 40. You can save her, but you'll have to prove something to her first.
gods.thorgrim_desc: The god of justice on floor 55 turned into a tyrant. His arguments are technically correct and completely mad. You can try to reason with him.
gods.noctura_desc: She's on floor 70. You've been meeting her in disguise all game, and she arranged much of what happened to you.
gods.aurelion_desc: He is down on floor 85. Lies told in the world above weaken him, and by the time you reach him he can barely speak.
gods.terravok_desc: He is the oldest of the seven and has been asleep on floor 95 for a very long time. You can wake him, but whether you should is the question.
gods.manwe_desc: Manwe made everything, but at the bottom on floor 100 he is tired of existing and does not want to fight. He asks you a question. You settle things by a fight, saving him, or an alliance. Everything you did on the way down decides your ending. I spent the most time writing this encounter.
classes.title: CLASSES & RACES
classes.subtitle: 12 classes + 5 prestige classes, 10 races. Pick whatever sounds fun. They all play differently.
classes.prestige_desc: Unlocked by completing different endings. Each has both spells and combat abilities.
classes.warrior_desc: The default pick. Decent at everything. Not going to blow anyone away but won't let you down either.
classes.paladin_desc: Tanky. Lots of stamina, strong defense. Good if you want to not die.
classes.ranger_desc: Quick, versatile. High stamina and dex. Good all-arounder for people who want to explore the dungeon without worrying too much about builds.
classes.assassin_desc: Highest dex in the game and the backstab mechanic is devastating when it lands. You will die fast if something connects though. High risk, high reward.
classes.bard_desc: High charisma so NPCs treat you better. Can do a bit of everything. Not amazing at any one thing but you'll never feel useless.
classes.jester_desc: Fastest thing on two legs. Max agility and dex. The abilities are chaotic and weird. Fun class if you don't mind some randomness.
classes.alchemist_desc: Sort of a wizard-scientist hybrid. High INT and WIS. The abilities have a crafting flavor to them.
classes.magician_desc: The full spellcaster. Access to all 25 arcane spells. Will destroy things with magic, but if a monster actually reaches you in melee you're in trouble.
classes.cleric_desc: Healing and support magic. Can hold their own in a fight too. In multiplayer, everybody wants a cleric in the party.
classes.sage_desc: Biggest mana pool in the game (50 base). Highest WIS and INT. You'll cast spells all day while the magician ran out three fights ago.
classes.barbarian_desc: Biggest numbers in the game. Most HP, most strength, most stamina. Basically just walks forward and hits things. INT stat is there technically.
classes.shaman_desc: Melee-caster hybrid, locked to Troll, Orc, and Gnoll. Enchants its weapon with the elements and plants totems that keep working while it swings. Fights up close and casts at the same time.
classes.tidesworn_desc: The Ocean's divine shield. Channel primordial waters as a holy tank and healer. Unlocked by the Savior ending.
classes.wavecaller_desc: Conductor of the Ocean's harmonics. Amplify allies with powerful buffs and healing. Unlocked by the Savior ending.
classes.cyclebreaker_desc: Exploits the seams between cycles to bend probability and time. Unlocked by the Defiant ending.
classes.abysswarden_desc: Warden of the Old Gods' prisons. Siphon divine corruption as weapon and sustain. Unlocked by the Usurper ending.
classes.voidreaver_desc: Consumer of the void between cycles. Sacrifice your own life force for devastating power. Unlocked by the Usurper ending.
classes.human_desc: Middle of the road. No restrictions, no weaknesses, no standout strengths. Safe pick.
classes.hobbit_desc: Harder to kill than you'd expect from something that short. Low STR though.
classes.elf_desc: The caster race. Lower HP but better magic stats and good agility. Pick this if you're going Magician or Sage.
classes.halfelf_desc: A bit of human, a bit of elf. Good stamina. Nothing flashy.
classes.dwarf_desc: Most HP, most STR, most DEF. The tank race. Short, stubborn, will outlast anything.
classes.troll_desc: Huge. Can't be every class but the stats are hard to argue with. Dwarf-tier tankiness with even more raw strength.
classes.orc_desc: Natural fighter. Not charming. Gets the job done.
classes.gnome_desc: Small, clever, modest stats. They work better than they look on paper.
classes.gnoll_desc: Smallest race. Makes up for it with determination and surprisingly decent STR.
classes.mutant_desc: Weird one. The bonuses are random-ish so every mutant plays a little different. Pick this if you like surprises.
companions.title: COMPANIONS
companions.subtitle: You can recruit five companions who fight beside you in the dungeon. Each one has a personal quest line, and they can die for good.
companions.lyris_desc: She is a traveler with silver streaks in her hair who watches you like she knows something you do not. She speaks in riddles, and you can romance her.
companions.lyris_backstory: She used to guard the Deepwood before corruption ruined the forest and changed its creatures into monsters. She was the only survivor. She headed underground to follow the corruption to its source and retrieve a mother-tree seed.
companions.aldric_desc: Aldric is an old soldier covered in scars. He doesn't talk much about where they came from. You recruit him at level 10 as your earliest companion, and he serves as your tank.
companions.aldric_backstory: He used to lead the King's Guard as captain until a demon slaughtered his entire squad. He was the only one who lived, and his quest forces him to confront that demon.
companions.aldric_quote: "I've failed people before. I won't fail you."
companions.mira_desc: Mira is a former priestess you recruit at level 20 to keep your party alive. Her faith shattered after her temple was destroyed, but she continues healing because she knows nothing else.
companions.mira_backstory: She spent her life healing in Veloura's temple. When Veloura became corrupted, the healers turned on each other and Mira escaped. Her quest builds toward a decision on whether healing people is still worth doing.
companions.mira_quote: "I heal because I don't know what else to do. Is that enough?"
companions.vex_desc: Vex is a thief and the last companion you can recruit. He joins at level 25 after helping you escape from prison. He deals damage, he's quick with his hands and always has something to say, and he jokes about everything including dying.
companions.vex_backstory: A wasting illness has been slowly killing him since birth. His quest One More Sunrise works through a list of things he wants done before dying. He dies 30 real days after you recruit him, and nothing in the game stops it.
companions.vex_quote: "Life's too short to take seriously. Trust me, I know."
companions.melodia_desc: Melodia runs the Music Shop and joins your party at level 20. Her songs heal and strengthen your party. She knows more about the Old Gods than she lets on, and you can romance her.
companions.melodia_backstory: She once traveled with a famous adventuring party and wrote songs about them. They fell one by one in the dungeon, so she opened her shop. Her quest The Lost Opus is to recover a legendary musical score deep in the dungeon.
companions.melodia_quote: "Every song needs an ending. Even mine."
endings.title: FIVE ENDINGS
endings.subtitle: Won't say much about these. They're better if you find them yourself.
endings.usurper_desc: Take the power. Become god. Get everything you wanted. Live with the consequences of "everything" lasting forever.
endings.savior_desc: Fix the gods. Heal what was broken. Everyone calls you a hero and that sounds great until you realize what that obligation actually means long-term.
endings.defiant_desc: Smash all of it. Walk away. No gods, no power, just a person.
endings.awakening_desc: Requires NG+. You start to see the loop for what it is. This ending only makes sense if you've been through the cycle more than once.
endings.dissolution_desc: Cycle 3 or later. The secret one. Hardest to reach. Quietest. I'm not going to describe it here.
history.title: HISTORY
history.subtitle: Usurper started as a BBS door game and became Usurper Reborn.
history.bbs_desc: Before the web, people ran Bulletin Board Systems. A BBS was a computer you dialed into with a modem over the phone line. You heard the screech of the handshake when you connected. Inside were ANSI art screens and games. By 1992, there were over 25,000 BBSes in the US. A SysOp ran each one from a basement or a bedroom.
history.doors_desc: Door games were outside programs a BBS launched for callers. They were all text and ran over a phone line. You had limited play time per day. Trade Wars 2002 and Legend of the Red Dragon had persistent worlds. What one caller did today changed what other players found tomorrow.
history.usurper_desc: Jakob Dangarden wrote Usurper in Turbo Pascal in 1993. Legend of the Red Dragon was the big door game then, but Usurper was more complex. It had races and classes with real differences. It had a 100 level dungeon, team warfare and a throne you could take. It was set in Dorashire with the Dungeons of Durunghins. Devoted players followed it through updates into the early 2000s.
history.alive_desc:
Jakob Dangarden released Usurper under the GPL in 2004.

Rick Parrish of R&M Software ported the Pascal source to modern systems for 32 and 64 bit. He also wrote GameSrv, which is BBS server software.

Daniel Zingaro did a large part of the bug fixing on the Pascal source. Version 0.20e is the most stable release because of it.
history.reborn_desc:
I'm Jason Knight. I started Usurper Reborn in 2024 to see what Usurper could be without the limits of 1990s hardware. I wrote it in C# on .NET 8.0, and all the original gameplay is in it.

I added about 60 unique NPCs with companions and a world simulation that runs on the server 24/7 whether anyone is logged in. You get New Game+ where NPCs become aware of the loop. There are seven god encounters with branching dialogue and five endings. The game still runs as a door game on BBSes.
connect.title: PLAY
connect.browser_desc: The browser option opens a full-page terminal in a new tab, with no installation needed.
connect.ssh_desc: We recommend SSH, which works from your terminal or a MUD client that speaks SSH.
connect.telnet_desc: Telnet is for MUD clients that don't do SSH. It's unencrypted but works fine.
connect.telnet_auth: No password needed / login or register at the welcome screen
connect.download_desc: Standalone builds run on Windows, Linux, and macOS. You can play offline or connect to the online server.
connect.steam_desc: You can get Usurper Reborn on Steam with a terminal and the fonts bundled in.
connect.observatory_desc: The Observatory is a live dashboard of the town's NPCs. It displays personality charts, relationship maps, population figures, and live events.
bbs.title: BBS LIST
bbs.subtitle: BBSes that are running Usurper Reborn as a door game right now.
bbs.note: Running Usurper Reborn on your board? Let me know and I'll add you.
credits.title: CREDITS
credits.jakob_desc: Wrote Usurper in Turbo Pascal. JAS Software. Made the decision to GPL it in 2004 which is the only reason any of this is possible.
credits.rick_desc: Ported the original Pascal to modern systems. Created GameSrv. If you've played a door game in the last 15 years, Rick's software was probably involved.
credits.daniel_desc: Went through the 1993 Pascal source line by line fixing bugs nobody else had bothered to track down. v0.20e is the stable version because of his work.
credits.jason_desc: That's me. Built the C# remake, wrote all the story content, the NPC system, the world sim, the god encounters. Still actively developing it.
credits.xbit_desc: Race and class portrait art seen during character creation. Beautiful ANSI art from x-bit.org.
credits.sudden_desc: Creator of rez2ans, the ANSI conversion tool used to bring portrait art into the game.
credits.cozmo_desc: ANSI art knowledge and guidance from Lunatics Unleashed.
credits.fastfinge_desc: Community contributor helping improve the codebase.
credits.maxsond_desc: Community contributor helping improve the codebase.
credits.lowleveljavacoder_desc: Community contributor helping improve the codebase across many systems.
credits.coosh_desc: Community contributor. Found and fixed an XP-formula desync regression by tracing his own soft-locked Lv.73 character to 12 duplicated copies of the same function across the codebase, then centralizing them into one canonical implementation.
credits.testingbytes_desc: Community contributor helping polish the game's menus.
credits.thanks: Thanks to every SysOp who kept a board running, and every kid who dialed in to explore Durunghins.
footer.desc: Usurper Reborn: a free, open-source remake of Usurper (1993) by Jakob Dangarden.
footer.tech: GPL v2 • C# / .NET 8.0 • Made by one person who liked BBS games too much
r1.hero_desc: The town of Dorashire goes on without you: its people marry, raise children, grow old, and remember what you did to them. Death here is permanent, and a hundred floors below the streets, seven broken gods are waiting.
r1.live_online: adventurers in the world right now
r1.cta_note: Play free in your browser. There's nothing to download or install.
r1.hero_nostalgia: Usurper was a 1993 BBS door game you played by dialing in with a modem. In Reborn's online game, death is permanent once your lives run out, and the dungeon gets harder from floor 25 down.
r1.stats_sub: These statistics update every few minutes from the running online server. You can follow town events in the news feed, and deaths appear there too.
r1.world_sub: The town keeps going while you're away, and people remember what you've done to them.
r1.w1t: Townspeople live on their own schedule
r1.w1d: Townspeople have personalities, goals and memories. They shop, train, fall in love, start fights and go into the dungeon whether anyone's logged in or not.
r1.w2d: If you kill someone in town, their living relatives hold it against you, including their children and siblings. In New Game+, people start to recognize you from earlier cycles, and that recognition grows each time.
r1.w3d: Townspeople marry, have children, grow old, and die of old age. Their children grow up into new townspeople. You can marry and have children too. How you raise them shapes the adults they become. If your character dies for good, your eldest adult child inherits half your gold.
r1.w4d: Online you have a small number of lives. Lose the last one and the character is deleted. The town news reports it. Your name goes into the Hall of the Fallen at the Temple. Your next character starts with an heirloom gift of gold that grows with the dead character's level.
r1.w5t: The gods want to talk first
r1.w5d: Seven god bosses wait on the way down. Each talks before the fight, and what you answer changes that fight. The one at the bottom of floor 100 doesn't want to fight. He asks you a question, but the ending comes from the choices you made on the way down.
r1.w6d: The game keeps a running chronicle of marriages, murders, births and coups. Open “Live statistics” under More, further down the page, to watch it as it happens.
r1.world_footer: It's built on the 1993 original, with 12 classes, 10 races and 100 spells counting the prestige classes. You get throne politics, factions, PvP, a shared economy and a 100-floor dungeon that gets harder floor by floor from floor 25.
r1.classes_sub: You start with 12 classes, and the game doesn't rank any of them above the others.
r1.cl_warrior: Warrior: stronger basic attacks and taunts
r1.cl_paladin: Paladin: guards the party and hits undead and demons harder
r1.cl_barbarian: Barbarian: Rage boosts attacks and lowers defense
r1.cl_cleric: Cleric: stronger healing from spells and abilities
r1.cl_bard: Bard: strengthens teammates with songs and inspiration
r1.cl_jester: Jester: random lucky breaks in fights
r1.cl_alchemist: Alchemist: stronger healing potions and thrown bombs
r1.cl_shaman: Mystic Shaman: totems and elemental weapon enchants
r1.classes_races: Races: Human, Elf, Half-Elf, Dwarf, Troll, Orc, Gnome, Gnoll, Hobbit, Mutant. Yes, Mutant. Trolls regenerate. Gnolls bite.
r1.classes_prestige: There are five prestige classes: Tidesworn, Wavecaller, Cyclebreaker, Abysswarden and Voidreaver. The endings you've reached decide which ones you can choose in New Game+.
r1.endings_sub: I didn't list the endings here on purpose.
r1.endings_desc: There are five endings. You settle things with Manwe on floor 100 by fighting him, saving him or forming an alliance. You don't pick an ending from a menu. Your choices across the game decide it, including how good or evil you've been and which Old Gods you saved or destroyed. One secret ending only becomes available from cycle three onward.
r1.endings_close: Most endings unlock prestige classes for your next life. One ends the loop instead.
r1.road_sub: The source code and issue tracker are public on GitHub. This roadmap shows what's shipped and what's planned:
r1.road_now_d: 1.3.8 is out: you can tell an ally to wait in a cleared dungeon room, allies who see a teammate finished remember it, and a single player load now starts from a clean story, with NPC opinions and companion settings kept as they were saved. Fixes to the stance menu, the news, saves, the SSH relay and the English spelling round it out. The roadmap below says what comes next.
r1.road_136_d: Shipped: five enchant rules (a real magic resistance, poison over several rounds, Titan's Resolve for max HP, enchants for companions, abilities, PvP and world bosses, and stronger Phoenix Fire and Frostbite), and an audit of every ability and spell of all seventeen classes, with 79 changes in all so each does what its text says.
r1.road_138_d: Shipped: an order to tell an ally to wait in a cleared room, allies who remember a fallen teammate, single player loads that start clean, NPC opinions that hold across a load and an SSH relay that keeps the game's last lines, with 11 changes in all.
r1.road_137_d: Shipped: the classes tuned from the measurements of every class at every depth and against every Old God (Power Hat, the Alchemist's late bombs, the Voidreaver's Constitution and Corruption Harvest), harder monsters on floors 76 to 100, and Manwe's Creator's Ward against gear enchantments, with 18 changes in all.
r1.road_20_d: A graphical client for the same living world, grown from the one that already runs in the repository.
r1.road_beyond_d: More languages. And more of the world growing on its own: settlements, wilderness, families, townsfolk on the online server who fight, talk and travel with more sense, and whatever the simulation surprises us with next. Bring ideas to Discord; they have a habit of shipping with your name in the release notes.
r1.road_135_d: Shipped: counter enchants against the last three Old Gods, Maelketh scaled to party size and Manwe made winnable for a full party with Godbane, many enchant and loot effect fixes, and reworked gear crit damage, regeneration and armor piercing. Dungeon floors 11 to 34 were measured and kept as they are; how gear grows from floor to floor is measured and tuned with the classes in 1.3.6 and 1.3.7.
r1.road_134_t: 1.3.4: Password reset and the Old Gods measured
r1.road_134_d: Shipped: you can reset a forgotten password by email, and the Old God fights and prestige classes were measured, with fixes where a spell or a god did not do what its text said.
r1.road_133_d: Shipped: dungeon floors 25 to 100 grow harder with depth and are built for a full team of five, and allies at 0 HP are Downed, can be rescued with a potion and are lost only when a monster finishes them.
r1.comm_sub: Players report bugs and suggest ideas on Discord. Come tell us how you died.
r1.sponsors_sub: The game is free and GPL licensed. These people help pay for the server. Thank you.
r1.finale_line1: Manwe, the god who made everything, waits on floor 100 with a question for you.
r1.finale_line2: Your choices decide the ending. Townspeople and their relatives remember what you did to them.
mail.footer: Usurper Reborn, {site}. This mail was sent because of a request on the game server; you do not need to reply.
mail.reset.subject: Reset your Usurper Reborn password
mail.reset.body:
Someone asked to reset the password of the account {name}.

To choose a new password, open this link within {minutes} minutes. It works once:
{link}

If you did not ask for this, ignore this mail. Your password stays the same.
mail.verify.subject: Confirm your email address for Usurper Reborn
mail.verify.body:
Someone asked to use this address for the account {name}.

To confirm it, open this link within {hours} hours:
{link}

If you did not ask for this, ignore this mail. The address is not added.
mail.linked.subject: This address is already linked to a Usurper Reborn account
mail.linked.body:
Someone asked to add this address to a Usurper Reborn account, but it is already linked to another account. Nothing was changed.

To use it on a different account, first remove it from the old account in the game (E on the character screen).
mail.change.subject: The email address on your Usurper Reborn account was changed
mail.change.body:
The email address on the account {name} was changed to a new one, and password resets now go there.

If you did not do this, log in to the game and change your password at once (P on the character screen).
mail.remove.subject: Your email address was removed from Usurper Reborn
mail.remove.body:
This address was removed from the account {name}. It no longer gets password reset links for that account.

If you did not do this, log in to the game and change your password at once (P on the character screen).
mail.changed.subject: Your Usurper Reborn password was changed
mail.changed.body:
The password of the account {name} was changed with a reset link. Every saved login of the account has ended, and the game server has closed its open sessions.

If you did not do this, ask for a new reset link at {site}/account/forgot at once.
account.forgot.title: Forgotten password
account.forgot.intro: Type your account name or the email address on your account. If the account has a confirmed email address, a reset link is sent to it. The link works for 30 minutes.
account.forgot.label: Account name or email address
account.forgot.sent: If that account has a confirmed email address, a reset link is on its way. Check your mail, including the spam folder.
account.forgot.empty: Type an account name or an email address.
account.forgot.bbs: Players who play through a BBS sign in with the BBS and have no game password here.
account.reset.title: Choose a new password
account.reset.label: New password
account.reset.done: Your password is changed. Every saved login has ended, and any open game session on this server is closed. Log in with the new password.
account.reset.bbs: A game played as a BBS door runs on that BBS, not on this server, and is not closed.
account.reset.short: The password needs at least 8 characters.
account.reset.colon: The password cannot contain a colon (:).
account.reset.mismatch: The two passwords are not the same.
account.invalid: This link is not valid any more. It may have been used already, or it has expired. Ask for a new one.
account.error: Something went wrong. Please try again in a few minutes.
account.mail_off: This server does not send mail. Ask the server's operator to reset your password.
account.verify.title: Confirm your email address
account.verify.intro: Press the button to confirm the address this link was sent to.
account.verify.done: Thank you. The request is complete. If the address could not be added, a mail to it explains why.
play.combat.idle: No fight right now. When one starts, it shows here.
play.chat.hint: Tells, gossip, shouts and guild lines from other players land here and stay when the screen redraws. Your own lines are not shown here. Type /history in the game to see the last 50 messages, your own included.
